3	description: Learn how to use the use server directive to execute code on the server.
4	---
5	
6	The `use server` directive designates a function or file to be executed on the **server side**. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all functions in the file are server-side, or inline at the top of a function to mark the function as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This is a React feature.
7	
8	## Using `use server` at the top of a file
9	
10	The following example shows a file with a `use server` directive at the top. All functions in the file are executed on the server.
11	
12	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
13	'use server'
14	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
15	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
16	
17	export async function createUser(data: { name: string; email: string }) {
18	  const session = await auth()
19	  if (!session?.user) {
20	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
21	  }
22	
23	  const user = await db.user.create({ data })
24	  return { id: user.id, name: user.name }
25	}
26	```
27	
28	```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1} switcher
29	'use server'
30	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
31	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
32	
33	export async function createUser(data) {
34	  const session = await auth()
35	  if (!session?.user) {
36	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
37	  }
38	
39	  const user = await db.user.create({ data })
40	  return { id: user.id, name: user.name }
41	}
42	```
43	
44	### Using Server Functions in a Client Component
45	
46	To use Server Functions in Client Components you need to create your Server Functions in a dedicated file using the `use server` directive at the top of the file. These Server Functions can then be imported into Client and Server Components and executed.
47	
48	Assuming you have a `fetchUsers` Server Function in `actions.ts`:
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
51	'use server'
52	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
53	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
54	
55	export async function fetchUsers() {
56	  const session = await auth()
57	  if (!session?.user) {
58	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
59	  }
60	
61	  const users = await db.user.findMany({
62	    select: { id: true, name: true, email: true },
63	  })
64	  return users
65	}
66	```

75	  if (!session?.user) {
76	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
77	  }
78	
79	  const users = await db.user.findMany({
80	    select: { id: true, name: true, email: true },
81	  })
82	  return users
83	}
84	```

86	Then you can import the `fetchUsers` Server Function into a Client Component and execute it on the client-side.
87	
88	```tsx filename="app/components/my-button.tsx" highlight={1,2,5} switcher
89	'use client'
90	import { fetchUsers } from '../actions'
91	
92	export default function MyButton() {

94	}
95	```

103	}
104	```

106	## Using `use server` inline
107	
108	In the following example, `use server` is used inline at the top of a function to mark it as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions):
109	
110	```tsx filename="app/posts/[id]/page.tsx" switcher highlight={8}
111	import { EditPost } from './edit-post'
112	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
113	
114	export default async function PostPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
115	  const post = await getPost(params.id)
116	
117	  async function updatePost(formData: FormData) {
118	    'use server'
119	    // Verify auth before saving (e.g. inside savePost)
120	    await savePost(params.id, formData)
121	    revalidatePath(`/posts/${params.id}`)
122	  }
123	
124	  return <EditPost updatePostAction={updatePost} post={post} />
125	}
126	```

148	Design your data access functions as secure primitives: validate inputs, check authentication and authorization, and constrain return types to only what the caller needs. When Server Functions delegate to a [Data Access Layer](/docs/app/guides/data-security#using-a-data-access-layer-for-mutations), these guarantees live in one place and apply consistently.

153	
154	Always authenticate and authorize users before performing sensitive server-side operations. Read authentication from cookies or headers rather than accepting tokens as function parameters.

160	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' // Your authentication library
161	
162	export async function createUser(data: { name: string; email: string }) {
163	  const session = await auth()
164	  if (!session?.user) {
165	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
166	  }
167	  const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
168	  return { id: newUser.id, name: newUser.name }
169	}

176	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' // Your authentication library
177

182	  }
183	  const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
184	  return { id: newUser.id, name: newUser.name }
185	}

The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 458 459 ```ts 460 // Before 461 revalidateTag('posts') 462 463 // After 464 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 465 ``` 466 467 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 468 469 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 470 'use server' 471 472 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 473 474 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 475 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 476 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 481 'use server' 482 483 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 484 485 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 486 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 487 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 488 } 489 ``` 490 491 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1150 } 1151 ``` 1152 1153 **After (Next.js 16):** 1154 1155 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1156 1157 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1158 async function fetchData() { 1159 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1160 // Use for server-side operations only 1161 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1162 } 1163 1164 export default async function Page() { 1165 const data = await fetchData() 1166 return
{/* render data */}
1167 } 1168 ``` 1169 1170 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1171 1172 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1173 1174 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1175 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1176 ``` 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1179 'use client' 1180 1181 export default function ClientComponent() { 1182 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1183 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1184 } 1185 ``` 1186 1187 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1188 1189 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1190 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1191 1192 export default async function Page() { 1193 await connection() 1194 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1195 return

{config}

1196 } 1197 ``` 1198 1199 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1200 1201 ### `devIndicators` Options 1202 1203 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1204 1205 - `appIsrStatus` 1206 - `buildActivity` 1207 - `buildActivityPosition` 1208 1209 The indicator itself remains available. 1210 1211 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1212 1213 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are deprecated. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 411 412 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 413 414 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 415 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 416 417 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 418 reactCompiler: true, 419 } 420 421 export default nextConfig 422 ``` 423 424 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 425 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 426 const nextConfig = { 427 reactCompiler: true, 428 } 429 430 module.exports = nextConfig 431 ``` 432 433 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 434 435 ```bash package="pnpm" 436 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 437 ``` 438 439 ```bash package="npm" 440 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 441 ``` 442 443 ```bash package="yarn" 444 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 445 ``` 446 447 ```bash package="bun" 448 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 449 ``` 450 451 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 452 453 ## Caching APIs 454 455 ### revalidateTag 456 457 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 458 459 ```ts 460 // Before 461 revalidateTag('posts') 462 463 // After 464 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 465 ``` 466 467 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 468 469 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 470 'use server' 471 472 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 473 474 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 475 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 476 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 481 'use server' 482 483 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 484 485 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 486 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 487 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 488 } 489 ``` 490 491 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 492 493 ### updateTag 494 495 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 496 497 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 498 499 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 513 'use server' 514 515 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 516 517 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 518 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 519 520 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 521 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 522 } 523 ``` 524 525 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 526 527 Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 528 529 ### refresh 530 531 [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 532 533 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 534 'use server' 535 536 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 537 538 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 539 // Update the notification in the database 540 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 541 542 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 543 refresh() 544 } 545 ``` 546 547 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 548 'use server' 549 550 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 551 552 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 553 // Update the notification in the database 554 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 555 556 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 557 refresh() 558 } 559 ``` 560 561 Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 562 563 ### cacheLife and cacheTag 564 565 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 566 567 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 568 569 ```ts 570 import { 571 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 572 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 573 } from 'next/cache' 574 ``` 575 576 You can update your imports to: 577 578 ```ts 579 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 580 ``` 581 582 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 583 584 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 592 593 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 594 595 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 596 597 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 598 599 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 600 601 ```js filename="next.config.js" 602 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 603 const nextConfig = { 604 cacheComponents: true, 605 } 606 607 module.exports = nextConfig 608 ``` 609 610 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 611 612 ```js filename="next.config.js" 613 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 614 const nextConfig = { 615 // If you are using PPR today 616 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 617 experimental: { 618 ppr: true, 619 }, 620 } 621 622 module.exports = nextConfig 623 ``` 624 625 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 626 627 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 628 629 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 630 631 ```bash filename="Terminal" 632 # Rename your middleware file 633 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 634 # or 635 mv middleware.js proxy.js 636 ``` 637 638 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 639 640 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 641 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 642 ``` 643 644 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 645 export function proxy(request) {} 646 ``` 647 648 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 649 650 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 651 652 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 653 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 654 655 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 656 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 657 } 658 659 export default nextConfig 660 ``` 661 662 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 663 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 664 const nextConfig = { 665 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 666 } 667 668 module.exports = nextConfig 669 ``` 670 671 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 672 673 ## `next/image` changes 674 675 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 676 677 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 678 679 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 680 import Image from 'next/image' 681 682 export default function Page() { 683 return 684 } 685 ``` 686 687 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 688 689 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 690 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 691 692 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 693 images: { 694 localPatterns: [ 695 { 696 pathname: '/assets/**', 697 search: '?v=1', 698 }, 699 ], 700 }, 701 } 702 703 export default nextConfig 704 ``` 705 706 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 707 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 708 const nextConfig = { 709 images: { 710 localPatterns: [ 711 { 712 pathname: '/assets/**', 713 search: '?v=1', 714 }, 715 ], 716 }, 717 } 718 719 module.exports = nextConfig 720 ``` 721 722 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 723 724 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 725 726 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 760 761 If you need to support 16px images: 762 763 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 764 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 765 766 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 767 images: { 768 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 769 }, 770 } 771 772 export default nextConfig 773 ``` 774 775 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 776 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 777 const nextConfig = { 778 images: { 779 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 780 }, 781 } 782 783 module.exports = nextConfig 784 ``` 785 786 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 787 788 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 789 790 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 791 792 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 793 794 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 795 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 796 797 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 798 images: { 799 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 800 }, 801 } 802 803 export default nextConfig 804 ``` 805 806 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 807 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 808 const nextConfig = { 809 images: { 810 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 811 }, 812 } 813 814 module.exports = nextConfig 815 ``` 816 817 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 818 819 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 820 821 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 822 823 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 824 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 825 826 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 827 images: { 828 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 829 }, 830 } 831 832 export default nextConfig 833 ``` 834 835 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 836 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 837 const nextConfig = { 838 images: { 839 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 840 }, 841 } 842 843 module.exports = nextConfig 844 ``` 845 846 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 847 848 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 849 850 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 851 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 852 853 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 854 images: { 855 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 856 // or 857 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 858 }, 859 } 860 861 export default nextConfig 862 ``` 863 864 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 865 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 866 const nextConfig = { 867 images: { 868 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 869 // or 870 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 871 }, 872 } 873 874 module.exports = nextConfig 875 ``` 876 877 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 878 879 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 880 881 ```tsx 882 // Before 883 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 884 885 // After 886 import Image from 'next/image' 887 ``` 888 889 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 890 891 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // image.domains is deprecated 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 domains: ['example.com'], 898 }, 899 } 900 ``` 901 902 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 903 904 ```js filename="next.config.js" 905 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 906 module.exports = { 907 images: { 908 remotePatterns: [ 909 { 910 protocol: 'https', 911 hostname: 'example.com', 912 }, 913 ], 914 }, 915 } 916 ``` 917 918 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 919 920 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 921 922 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 923 924 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 925 926 ```bash package="pnpm" 927 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 928 ``` 929 930 ```bash package="npm" 931 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 932 ``` 933 934 ```bash package="yarn" 935 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 936 ``` 937 938 ```bash package="bun" 939 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack 940 ``` 941 942 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 943 944 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 945 946 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 947 948 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 949 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 950 951 export default function Default() { 952 notFound() 953 } 954 ``` 955 956 Or return `null`: 957 958 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 959 export default function Default() { 960 return null 961 } 962 ``` 963 964 ## ESLint Flat Config 965 966 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 967 968 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 969 970 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 971 972 ## Scroll Behavior Override 973 974 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 975 976 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 977 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 978 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 979 980 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 981 982 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 983 984 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 985 986 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 987 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 988 return ( 989 990 {children} 991 992 ) 993 } 994 ``` 995 996 ## Performance Improvements 997 998 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 999 1000 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 1001 1002 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 1003 1004 ### `next dev` config load 1005 1006 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 1007 1008 - When running the `next dev` command 1009 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 1010 1011 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1012 1013 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1014 1015 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1016 1017 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1018 1019 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1020 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1021 1022 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1023 1024 if (isDev) { 1025 startServer() 1026 } 1027 1028 const nextConfig = { 1029 /* Your config options */ 1030 } 1031 1032 module.exports = nextConfig 1033 ``` 1034 1035 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1036 1037 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1038 1039 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1040 1041 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1042 1043 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1044 const nextConfig = { 1045 experimental: { 1046 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1047 }, 1048 } 1049 1050 module.exports = nextConfig 1051 ``` 1052 1053 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1054 1055 ## Modern Sass API 1056 1057 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1058 1059 ## Removals 1060 1061 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1062 1063 ### AMP Support 1064 1065 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1066 1067 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1068 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1069 1070 ```tsx 1071 // Removed 1072 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1073 1074 // Removed 1075 export const config = { amp: true } 1076 ``` 1077 1078 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1079 1080 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1081 const nextConfig = { 1082 // Removed 1083 amp: { 1084 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1085 }, 1086 } 1087 1088 export default nextConfig 1089 ``` 1090 1091 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1092 1093 ### `next lint` Command 1094 1095 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1096 1097 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1098 1099 ```bash package="pnpm" 1100 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1101 ``` 1102 1103 ```bash package="npm" 1104 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1105 ``` 1106 1107 ```bash package="yarn" 1108 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1109 ``` 1110 1111 ```bash package="bun" 1112 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1113 ``` 1114 1115 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1116 1117 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1118 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1119 const nextConfig = { 1120 // No longer supported 1121 // eslint: {}, 1122 } 1123 1124 export default nextConfig 1125 ``` 1126 1127 ### Runtime Configuration 1128 1129 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1130 1131 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1132 1133 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1134 module.exports = { 1135 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1136 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1137 }, 1138 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1139 apiUrl: '/api', 1140 }, 1141 } 1142 ``` 1143 1144 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1145 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1146 1147 export default function Page() { 1148 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1149 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1150 } 1151 ``` 1152 1153 **After (Next.js 16):** 1154 1155 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1156 1157 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1158 async function fetchData() { 1159 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1160 // Use for server-side operations only 1161 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1162 } 1163 1164 export default async function Page() { 1165 const data = await fetchData() 1166 return
{/* render data */}
1167 } 1168 ``` 1169 1170 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1171 1172 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1173 1174 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1175 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1176 ``` 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1179 'use client' 1180 1181 export default function ClientComponent() { 1182 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1183 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1184 } 1185 ``` 1186 1187 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1188 1189 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1190 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1191 1192 export default async function Page() { 1193 await connection() 1194 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1195 return

{config}

1196 } 1197 ``` 1198 1199 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1200 1201 ### `devIndicators` Options 1202 1203 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1204 1205 - `appIsrStatus` 1206 - `buildActivity` 1207 - `buildActivityPosition` 1208 1209 The indicator itself remains available. 1210 1211 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1212 1213 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are deprecated. Use top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) instead. 1214 1215 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1216 // Before: experimental.useCache 1217 module.exports = { 1218 experimental: { 1219 useCache: true, 1220 }, 1221 } 1222 ``` 1223 1224 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1225 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1226 module.exports = { 1227 experimental: { 1228 dynamicIO: true, 1229 }, 1230 } 1231 ``` 1232 1233 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1234 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1235 1236 // After 1237 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 1241 export default nextConfig 1242 ``` 1243 1244 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1245 // After 1246 module.exports = { 1247 cacheComponents: true, 1248 } 1249 ``` 1250 1251 For more on Cache Components, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). 1252 1253 ### `unstable_rootParams` 1254 1255 The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. We are working on an alternative API that we will ship in an upcoming minor release. 1256

1 --- 2 title: How to create forms with Server Actions 3 nav_title: Forms 4 description: Learn how to create forms in Next.js with React Server Actions. 5 --- 6 7 React Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions. 8 9 > [!WARNING] 10 > Always verify [authentication and authorization](/docs/app/guides/authentication) inside each Server Action, even if the form is only rendered on an authenticated page.
